terms.title: Natural history study
terms.tip: A study that follows people over time without testing a drug, to see how the disease changes. Later trials use that record.

terms.title: Predictive testing
terms.tip: A gene test in a person who has no symptoms, to learn whether they inherited an expansion.

terms.title: Autosomal dominant
terms.tip: One expanded copy is enough. Each child of a carrier has a 50% chance of inheriting it.

terms.title: CAG repeat
terms.tip: A run of the DNA letters C, A, and G. In ATXN3, an expanded run causes SCA3.

terms.title: Machado-Joseph disease
terms.tip: Another name for SCA3, from families described in the 1970s.

terms.title: Premanifest
terms.tip: A person who carries the expansion and does not yet have ataxia. Papers also say presymptomatic or pre-ataxic.

terms.title: Intrathecal
terms.tip: Given into the fluid around the spinal cord.

terms.title: Biomarker
terms.tip: A measurable sign, in a scan, blood, or spinal fluid, used to track a disease.

terms.title: NfL
terms.tip: Neurofilament light chain, a protein measured in blood or spinal fluid and studied as a marker of nerve injury.

terms.title: Anticipation
terms.tip: The repeat often grows when it is passed on, which can mean earlier symptoms in the next generation.

terms.title: PGT-M
terms.tip: Preimplantation genetic testing for a single-gene condition. Embryos from IVF can be tested for the familial expansion.

terms.title: Ataxin-3
terms.tip: The protein made by ATXN3. An expanded CAG repeat changes that protein.

terms.title: Penetrance
terms.tip: The chance that someone with a disease-causing genotype will develop the disease. The lower edge of full penetrance in SCA3 is uncertain.

terms.title: SCA3
terms.tip: Spinocerebellar ataxia type 3, also called Machado-Joseph disease, caused by an expanded CAG repeat in ATXN3.

terms.title: ASO
terms.tip: Antisense oligonucleotide: a short synthetic strand designed to bind a specific RNA.

terms.title: SARA
terms.tip: Scale for the Assessment and Rating of Ataxia. A clinician’s score of ataxia signs. Higher means more ataxia.
